solisequious: Following the course of the sun; as, solisequious plants. Sir T. Browne.
sopite: To lay asleep; to put to sleep; to quiet. (old) The king's declaration for the sopiting of all Arminian heresies. Fuller.
solemnness: The state or quality of being solemn; solemnity; impressiveness; gravity; as, the solemnness of public worship. [Written also solemness.]
sometime: 1. At a past time indefinitely referred to; once; formerly. Did they not sometime cry "All hail" to me Shak. 2. Talfourd.
sortable: 1. Capable of being sorted. 2. Suitable; befitting; proper. (old) con.
souarinut: The large edible nutlike seed of a tall tropical American tree (Caryocar nuciferum) of the same natural order with the tea plant; -- also called butternut. [Written also sawarra nut.]
sonship: The state of being a son, or of bearing the relation of a son; filiation. Dr. H. More.
southerliness: The quality or state of being southerly; direction toward the south.
solenacean: Any species of marine bivalve shells belonging to the family Solenidæ.
sottish: Like a sot; doltish; very foolish; drunken. How ignorant are sottish pretenders to astrology! Swift. Syn. -- Dull; stupid; senseless; doltish; infatuate. -- Sot"tish*ly, adv. -- Sot"tish*ness, n.
sonorous: 1. Giving sound when struck; resonant; as, sonorous metals. 2. Loud-sounding; giving a clear or loud sound; as, a sonorous voice. 3. Yielding sound; characterized by sound; vocal; sonant; as, the vowels are sonorous. 4. Impressive in sound; high-sounding.
sophistication: The act of sophisticating; adulteration; as, the sophistication of drugs. Boyle.
somniloquist: One who talks in his sleep.
solanaceous: Of or pertaining to plants of the natural order Solanaceæ, of which the nightshade (Solanum) is the type. The order includes also the tobacco, ground cherry, tomato, eggplant, red pepper, and many more.
socage: A tenure of lands and tenements by a certain or determinate service; a tenure distinct from chivalry or knight's service, in which the obligations were uncertain. sottovoce: 1. (Mus.) With a restrained voice or moderate force; in an undertone. 2. Spoken low or in an undertone.
solution: 1. The act of separating the parts of any body, or the condition of undergoing a separation of parts; disruption; breach. The act of solving, or the state of being solved; the disentanglement of any intricate problem or difficult question; explanation; clearing up;
solarium: 1. An apartment freely exposed to the sun; anciently, an apartment or inclosure on the roof of a house; in modern times, an apartment in a hospital, used as a resort for convalescents. 2. (Zoöl.) Any one of several species of handsome marine spiral shells of the genus Solarium and allied genera.
solemness: Solemnness. Some think he wanted solemnes. Sir H. Wotton.
socket: 1. An opening into which anything is fitted; any hollow thing or place which receives and holds something else; as, the sockets of the teeth. His eyeballs in their hollow sockets sink. Dryden. 2. Especially, the hollow tube or place in which a candle is fixed in the candlestick. And in the sockets oily bubbles dance. Dryden.
somatist: One who admits the existence of material beings only; a materialist. Glanvill.
sodamide: A greenish or reddish crystalline substance, NaNH2, obtained by passing ammonia over heated sodium.
soliloquize: To utter a soliloquy; to talk to one's self.
southeastern: Of or pertaining to the southeast; southeasterly.
soliform: Like the sun in form, appearance, or nature; resembling the sun. "Soliform things." Cudworth.
solpugid: Of or pertaining to the Solifugæ. -- n. One of the Solifugæ.
sontag: A knitted worsted jacket, worn over the waist of a woman's dress.
sorriness: The quality or state of being sorry.
sos: The letters signified by the signal ( . . . ---. . . ) prescribed by the International Radiotelegraphic Convention of 1912 for use by ships in distress.
solecist: One who commits a solecism. Blackwall.
soc: 1. (O. Eng. Law) (a) The lord's power or privilege of holding a court in a district, as in manor or lordship; jurisdiction of causes, and the limits of that jurisdiction. (b) Liberty or privilege of tenants excused from customary burdens. 2. An exclusive privilege formerly claimed by millers of grrinding all the corn used within the manor or township which the mill stands.
sobranje: The unicameral national assembly of Bulgaria, elected for a term of five years by universal suffrage of adult males.
soda: (a) Sodium oxide or hydroxide. (b) Popularly, sodium carbonate or bicarbonate. Caustic soda, sodium hydroxide. -- Cooking soda, sodium bicarbonate. [Colloq.] -- Sal soda. solarparallax: The parallax of the sun, that is, the angle subtended at the sun by the semidiameter of the earth. It is 8."80, and is the fundamental datum.
soja: An Asiatic leguminous herb (Glycine Soja) the seeds of which are used in preparing the sauce called soy.
soutane: A close garnment with straight sleeves, and skirts reaching to the ankles, and buttoned in front from top to bottom; especially, the black garment of this shape worn by the clergy in France and Italy as their daily dress; a cassock.
solidly: In a solid manner; densely; compactly; firmly; truly.
soot: A black substance formed by combustion, or disengaged from fuel in the process of combustion, which rises in fine particles, and adheres to the sides of the chimney or pipe conveying the smoke; | To cover or dress with soot; to smut with, or as with, soot; as, to soot land. Mortimer.
soler: A loft or garret. See Solar, n. Sir W. Scott.
southmost: Farthest toward the south; southernmost. Milton.
souter: A shoemaker; a cobbler. (old) Chaucer. There is no work better than another to please God: . . . to wash dishes, to be a souter, or an apostle, -- all is one. Tyndale.
soupcon: A suspicion; a suggestion; hence, a very small portion; a taste; as, coffee with a soupçon of brandy; a soupçon of coquetry.
sopition: The act of putting to sleep, or the state of being put to sleep; sleep. (old) Dementation and sopition of reason. Sir T. Browne.
sophism: The doctrine or mode of reasoning practiced by a sophist; hence, any fallacy designed to deceive. Let us first rid ourselves of sophisms, those of depraved men, and those of heartless philosophers. I. Taylor.
sordid: 1. Filthy; foul; dirty. (old) A sordid god; down from his hoary chin A length of beard descends, uncombed, unclean. Dryden. 2. Vile; base; gross; mean; as, vulgar, sordid mortals. soberness: The quality or state of being sober.
sowle: To pull by the ears; to drag about. (old) hak.
sonant: 1. Of or pertaining to sound; sounding. 2. (Phonetics) Uttered, as an element of speech, with tone or proper vocal sound, as distinguished from mere breath sound; intonated; voiced; tonic; the opposite of nonvocal, or surd;
sorely: In a sore manner; grievously; painfully; as, to be sorely afflicted.
sorrow: The uneasiness or pain of mind which is produced by the loss of any good, real or supposed, or by diseappointment in the expectation of good; grief at having suffered or occasioned evil; regret; | To feel pain of mind in consequence of evil experienced, feared, or done; to grieve; to be sad; to be sorry. Sorrowing most of all . . . that they should see his face no more. Acts xx. 38.
solidist: An advocate of, or believer in, solidism. Dunglison.
sophime: Sophism. (old) I trow ye study aboute some sophime. Chaucer.
solecism: 1. An impropriety or incongruity of language in the combination of words or parts of a sentence; esp., deviation from the idiom of a language or from the rules of syntax. somnambulation: The act of walking in sleep.
sothic: Of or pertaining to Sothis, the Egyptian name for the Dog Star; taking its name from the Dog Star; canicular. Sothiac, or Sothic, year (Chronol.), the Egyptian year of 365 days and 6 hours, as distinguished from the Egyptian vague year, which contained 365 days. soggy: Filled with water; soft with moisture; sodden; soaked; wet; as, soggy land or timber.
sonorific: Producing sound; as, the sonorific quality of a body. I. Watts.
somite: One of the actual or ideal serial segments of which an animal, esp. an articulate or vertebrate, is composed; somatome; metamere. -- So*mit`ic, a.
soutage: That in which anything is packed; bagging, as for hops. (old) Halliwell.
socager: A tennant by socage; a socman.
soaker: 1. One who, or that which, soaks. 2. A hard drinker. [Slang] South.
soreness: The quality or state of being sore; tenderness; painfull; as, the soreness of a wound; the soreness of an affliction.
somber: 1. Dull; dusky; somewhat dark; gloomy; as, a somber forest; a somber house. 2. Melancholy; sad; grave; depressing; as, a somber person; somber reflections. The dinner was silent and somber; | To make somber, or dark; to make shady.
solidification: Act of solidifying, or state of being solidified.
socialistic: Pertaining to, or of the nature of, socialism.
solacement: The act of solacing, or the state of being solaced; also, that which solaces.
sonance: 1. A sound; a tune; as, to sound the tucket sonance. (old) Shak. 2. The quality or state of being sonant.
sovran: A variant of Sovereign. (poetic) On thy bald, awful head, O sovran Blanc. Coleridge.
sorehead: One who is disgruntled by a failure in politics, or the like. [Slang, U.S.]
sorehon: Formerly, in Ireland, a kind of servile tenure which subjected the tenant to maintain his chieftain gratuitously whenever he wished to indulge in a revel. Spenser.
sophomore: One belonging to the second of the four classes in an American college, or one next above a freshman. [Formerly written also sophimore.]
solvability: 1. The quality or state of being solvable; as, the solvability of a difficulty; the solvability of a problem. 2. The condition of being solvent; ability to pay all just debts; solvency; as, the solvability of a merchant.
southeaster: A storm, strong wind, or gale coming from the southeast.
southernly: Somewhat southern. -- adv. In a southerly manner or course; southward.
so: 1. In that manner or degree; as, indicated (in any way), or as implied, or as supposed to be known. Why is his chariot so long in coming Judges v. 28. 2. sollar: 1. See Solar, n. (old) 2. (Mining) A platform in a shaft, especially one of those between the series of ladders in a shaft. | To cover, or provide with, a sollar.
solidness: 1. State or quality of being solid; firmness; compactness; solidity, as of material bodies. 2. Soundness; strength; truth; validity, as of arguments, reasons, principles, and the like.
solidago: A genus of yellow-flowered composite perennial herbs; golden- rod.
solacious: Affording solace; as, a solacious voice. (old) Bale.
sobriety: 1. Habitual soberness or temperance as to the use of spirituous liquors; as, a man of sobriety. Public sobriety is a relative duty. Blackstone. 2. sophistry: 1. The art or process of reasoning; logic. (old) 2. The practice of a sophist; fallacious reasoning; reasoning sound in appearance only. soft: 1. Easily yielding to pressure; easily impressed, molded, or cut; not firm in resisting; impressible; yielding; also, malleable; -- opposed to Ant: hard; as, a soft bed; a soft peach; soft earth; | A soft or foolish person; an idiot. [Colloq.] G. Eliot.
somatopleure: The outer, or parietal, one of the two lamellæ into which the vertebrate blastoderm divides on either side of the notochord, and from which the walls of the body and the amnion are developed. See Splanchopleure.
sorbite: A sugarlike substance, isomeric with mannite and dulcite, found with sorbin in the ripe berries of the sorb, and extracted as a sirup or a white crystalline substance. -- Sor*bit"ic, a.
sobriquet: An assumed name; a fanciful epithet or appellation; a nickname. [Sometimes less correctly written soubriquet.]
soiree: An evening party; -- distinguished from levee, and matinée.
soul: To afford suitable sustenance. (old) Warner. | 1. The spiritual, rational, and immortal part in man; that part of man which enables him to think, and which renders him a subject of moral government; -- sometimes, in distinction from the higher…
sonties: Probably from "saintes" saints, or from sanctities; -- used as an oath. (old) Shak.
solfa: To sing the notes of the gamut, ascending or descending; as, do or ut, re, mi, fa, sol, la, si, do, or the same in reverse order. Yet can I neither solfe ne sing. Piers Plowman. | The gamut, or musical scale. See Tonic sol-fa, under Tonic, n.

sorghe: The three-beared rocking, or whistlefish. [Prov. Eng.]
sombrero: A kind of broad-brimmed hat, worn in Spain and in Spanish America. Marryat.
soger: Var. of Soldier. [Dial. or Slang] R. H. Dana, Jr.
solarization: Injury of a photographic picture caused by exposing it for too long a time to the sun's light in the camera; burning; excessive insolation.
southernwood: A shrubby species of wormwood (Artemisia Abrotanum) having aromatic foliage. It is sometimes used in making beer.
sortita: 1. The air sung by any of the principal characters in an opera on entering. 2. A closing voluntary; a postlude.
sorcery: Divination by the assistance, or supposed assistance, of evil spirits, or the power of commanding evil spirits; magic; necromancy; witchcraft; enchantment. Adder's wisdom I have learned, To fence my ear against thy sorceries. Milton.
soam: A chain by which a leading horse draws a plow. Knight.
socalled: So named; called by such a name (but perhaps called thus with doubtful propriety).

something: 1. Anything unknown, undetermined, or not specifically designated; a certain indefinite thing; an indeterminate or unknown event; an unspecified task, work, or thing. soyned: Filled with care; anxious. (old) Mir. for Mag.
soldanel: A plant of the genus Soldanella, low Alpine herbs of the Primrose family.
somnipathist: A person in a state of somniapathy.

sourness: The quality or state of being sour.
softshell: Having a soft or fragile shell. Soft-shell clam (Zoöl.), the long clam. See Mya. -- Soft-shelled crab. (Zoöl.) See the Note under Crab, 1. -- Soft-shelled turtle. (Zoöl.) Same as Soft tortoise, under Soft.
soldiery: 1. A body of soldiers; soldiers, collectivelly; the military. A camp of faithful soldiery. Milton. 2. Military service. (old) Sir P. Sidney.
soberminded: Having a disposition or temper habitually sober. -- So"ber-mind`ed*ness, n.
solemn: 1. Marked with religious rites and pomps; enjoined by, or connected with, religion; sacred. His holy rites and solemn feasts profaned. Milton. Stately; ceremonious; grand.

somnipathy: Sleep from sympathy, or produced by mesmerism or the like. [Written also somnopathy.]

solver: One who, or that which, solves.

soundless: Not capable of being sounded or fathomed; unfathomable. Shak. | Having no sound; noiseless; silent. -- Sound"less*ly, adv. -- Sound"less*ness, n.
solely: Singly; alone; only; without another; as, to rest a cause solely one argument; to rely solelyn one's own strength.
sonnish: Like the sun; sunny; golden. (old) "Her sonnish hairs." Chaucer.
solstitial: 1. Of or pertaining to a solstice. 2. Happening at a solstice; esp. (with reference to the northern hemisphere), happening at the summer solstice, or midsummer. "Solstitial summer's heat." Milton.
southness: A tendency in the end of a magnetic needle to point toward the south pole. Faraday.

socman: One who holds lands or tenements by socage; a socager. Cowell.
sodiumsulphate: A salt well known as a catharic under the name of Glauber's salt, which term is properly applied to the hydrate, Na2SO4.10H2O.
soko: An African anthropoid ape, supposed to be a variety of the chimpanzee.
sociologic: Of or pertaining to sociology, or social science. -- So`ci*o*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
sounder: One who, or that which; sounds; specifically, an instrument used in telegraphy in place of a register, the communications being read by sound.
soilure: Stain; pollution. Shak. Then fearing rust or soilure, fashioned for it A case of silk. Tennyson.
sodomitical: Pertaining to, or of the nature of, sodomy. -- Sod`om*it"ic*al*ly, adv.
soudet: United; consolidated; made firm; strengthened. (old) O martyr souded for virginity! Chaucer.
sozzle: 1. To splash or wet carelessly; as, to sozzle the feet in water. [Local, U.S.] Bartlett. 2. To heap up in confusion. [Prov. Eng.] Forby. | 1. One who spills water or other liquids carelessly; specifically, a sluttish woman. [Local, U.S.] 2. A mass, or heap, confusedly mingled. [Prov. Eng.]

solenoglyph: Pertaining to the Selenoglypha. See Ophidia. -- n. One of the Selenoglypha.

soubrette: A female servant or attendant; specifically, as a term of the theater, a lady's maid, in comedies, who acts the part of an intrigante; a meddlesome, mischievous female servant or young woman.
solemnly: In a solemn manner; with gravity; seriously; formally. There in deaf murmurs solemnly are wise. Dryden. I do solemnly assure the reader. Swift.
souterrain: A grotto or cavern under ground. (old) Arbuthnot.
somehow: In one way or another; in some way not yet known or designated; by some means; as, the thing must be done somehow; he lives somehow. soorma: A preparation of antimony with which Mohammedan men anoint their eyelids.
softness: The quality or state of being soft; -- opposed to Ant: hardness, and used in the various specific senses of the adjective.
socialize: 1. To render social. 2. To subject to, or regulate by, socialism.
sonata: An extended composition for one or two instruments, consisting usually of three or four movements; as, Beethoven's sonatas for the piano, for the violin and piano, etc. Note: The same general structure prevails in symphonies, instrumental trios, quartets, etc., and even in classical concertos.
solidarity: An entire union or consolidation of interests and responsibilities; fellowship; community. solleret: A flexible steel shoe (or one of the plates forming such a shoe), worn with mediæval armor.
solitude: 1. state of being alone, or withdrawn from society; a lonely life; loneliness. Whosoever is delighted with solitude is either a wild beast or a god. Bacon. soteriology: 1. A discourse on health, or the science of promoting and preserving health. 2. (Theol.) The doctrine of salvation by Jesus Christ.
sovenaunce: Remembrance. (old) Of his way he had no sovenance. Spenser.
solarize: To injure by too long exposure to the light of the sun in the camera; to burn. | To become injured by undue or too long exposure to the sun's rays in the camera.
solitariety: The state of being solitary; solitariness. (old) Cudworth.

solutive: Tending to dissolve; loosening; laxative. Bacon.

somatopleuric: of or pertaining to the somatopleure.
sonifer: A kind of ear trumpet for the deaf, or the partially deaf.
sombrous: Gloomy; somber. "Tall and sombrous pines." Longfellow. -- Som"brous*ly, adv. -- Som"brous*ness, n.
sondeli: The musk shrew. See under Musk.
southward: Toward the south, or toward a point nearer the south than the east or west point; as, to go southward. | The southern regions or countries; the south. Sir W. Raleigh.
solidify: To make solid or compact. Every machine is a solidified mechanical theorem. H. Spencer.
socratic: Of or pertaining to Socrates, the Grecian sage and teacher. (b. c. 469-399), or to his manner of teaching and philosophizing. sorbefacient: Producing absorption. -- n. A medicine or substance which produces absorption.
sorbin: An unfermentable sugar, isomeric with glucose, found in the ripe berries of the rowan tree, or sorb, and extracted as a sweet white crystalline substance; -- called also mountain-ash sugar.

sorcerer: A conjurer; an enchanter; a magician. Bacon. Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers. Ex. vii. 11.
souther: A strong wind, gale, or storm from the south.
southerly: the old squaw; -- so called in imitation of its cry. Called also southerly, and southerland. See under Old.
sodic: Of or pertaining to sodium; containing sodium.
sock: 1. The shoe worn by actors of comedy in ancient Greece and Rome, -- used as a sumbol of comedy, of the comic drams, as distinguished from tragedy, which is symbolized by the buskin. Great Fletcher never treads in buskin here, Nor greater Jonson dares in socks appear. Dryden. 2. A knit or woven covering for the foot and lower leg; a stocking with a short leg. 3.
solanoid: Resembling a potato; -- said of a kind of cancer.
solanicine: An alkaloid produced by the action of hydrochloric acid on solanidine, as a tasteless yellow crystalline substance.
sore: Reddish brown; sorrel. Sore falcon. (Zoöl.) See Sore, n., 1. | A young hawk or falcon in the first year. 2. (Zoöl.) A young buck in the fourth year. See the Note under Buck.
soapy: 1. Resembling soap; having the qualities of, or feeling like, soap; soft and smooth. 2. Smeared with soap; covered with soap.
sophistic: Of or pertaining to a sophist; embodying sophistry; fallaciously subtile; not sound. His argument . . . is altogether sophistical. Macaulay. -- So*phis"tic*al*ly, adv. -- So*phis"tic*al*ness, n.
society: 1. The relationship of men to one another when associated in any way; companionship; fellowship; company. "Her loved society." Milton. There is society where none intrudes By the deep sea, and music in its roar. Byron. 2. Connection; participation; partnership. The meanest of the people and such as have the least society with the acts and crimes of kings. Jer. Taylor. 3.
soursop: The large succulent and slightly acid fruit of a small tree (Anona muricata) of the West Indies; also, the tree itself. It is closely allied to the custard apple.
somnial: Of or pertaining to sleep or dreams. The somnial magic superinducted on, without suspending, the active powers of the mind. Coleridge.
sodium: A common metallic element of the alkali group, in nature always occuring combined, as in common salt, in albite, etc. It is isolated as a soft, waxy, white, unstable metal, so readily oxidized that it combines violently with water, and to be preserved must be kept under petroleum or some similar liquid.
sonority: The quality or state of being sonorous; sonorousness.
soffit: The under side of the subordinate parts and members of buildings, such as staircases, entablatures, archways, cornices, or the like. See Illust. of Lintel.
sonnet: 1. A short poem, -- usually amatory. (old) Shak. He had a wonderful desire to chant a sonnet or hymn unto Apollo Pythius. Holland. 2. A poem of fourteen lines, -- two stanzas, called the octave,… | To compose sonnets. "Strains that come almost to sonneting." Milton.
soy: 1. A Chinese and Japanese liquid sauce for fish, etc., made by subjecting boiled beans (esp. soja beans), or beans and meal, to long fermentation and then long digestion in salt and water. 2. (Bot.) The soja, a kind of bean. See Soja.
sotadic: Pertaining to, or resembling, the lascivious compositions of the Greek poet Sotades. -- n. A Sotadic verse or poem.
sodality: 1. A fellowship or fraternity; a brotherhood. 2. (R.C.Ch.) Specifically, a lay association for devotion or for charitable purposes.
soothsaying: 1. A true saying; truth. (old) 2. The act of one who soothsays; the foretelling of events; the art or practice of making predictions. A damsel, possessed with a spirit of divination . . . which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying. Acts xvi. 16. 3. A prediction; a prophecy; a prognostication. Divinations and soothsayings and dreams are vain. Eclus. xxxiv. 5.
sorbet: A kind of beverage; sherbet. Smolett.
sorex: A genus of small Insectivora, including the common shrews.
soap: A substance which dissolves in water, thus forming a lather, and is used as a cleansing agent. Soap is produced by combining fats or oils with alkalies or alkaline earths, usually by boiling, and… | 1. To rub or wash over with soap. 2. To flatter; to wheedle. [Slang]
somniloquism: The act or habit of talking in one's sleep; somniloquy. Coleridge.
sod: That stratum of the surface of the soil which is filled with the roots of grass, or any portion of that surface; turf; sward. She there shall dress a sweeter sod Than Fancy's feet have ever trod. Collins.
somatic: 1. Of or pertaining to the body as a whole; corporeal; as, somatic death; somatic changes. 2. Of or pertaining to the wall of the body; somatopleuric; parietal; as, the somatic stalk of the yolk sac of an embryo. Somatic death. See the Note under Death, n., 1.
somnolent: Sleepy; drowsy; inclined to sleep. -- Som"no*lent*ly, adv. He had no eye for such phenomens, because he had a somnolent want of interest in them. De Quincey.
southron: An inhabitant of the more southern part of a country; formerly, a name given in Scotland to any Englishman.
somatocyst: A cavity in the primary nectocalyx of certain Siphonophora. See Illust. under Nectocalyx.
soberly: In a sober manner; temperately; cooly; calmly; gravely; seriously. | Grave; serious; solemn; sad. (old) [He] looked hollow and thereto soberly. Chaucer.
solidungula: A tribe of ungulates which includes the horse, ass, and related species, constituting the family Equidæ.
social: 1. Of or pertaining to society; relating to men living in society, or to the public as an aggregate body; as, social interest or concerns; social pleasure; social benefits; social happiness; social duties. "Social phenomena." J. S. Mill. 2. Ready or disposed to mix in friendly converse; companionable; sociable; as, a social person. 3. Consisting in union or mutual intercourse.
sonnetist: A sonneter, or sonneteer. Bp. Hall.
societarian: Of or pertaining to society; social. The all-sweeping besom of societarian reformation. Lamb.
softshelled: Having a soft or fragile shell. Soft-shell clam (Zoöl.), the long clam. See Mya. -- Soft-shelled crab. (Zoöl.) See the Note under Crab, 1. -- Soft-shelled turtle. (Zoöl.) Same as Soft tortoise, under Soft.
sorbonical: Belonging to the Sorbonne or to a Sorbonist. Bale.
sombre: 1. Dull; dusky; somewhat dark; gloomy; as, a somber forest; a somber house. 2. Melancholy; sad; grave; depressing; as, a somber person; somber reflections. The dinner was silent and somber; | To make somber, or dark; to make shady.
soil: To feed, as cattle or horses, in the barn or an inclosure, with fresh grass or green food cut for them, instead of sending them out to pasture; hence (such food having the effect of purging them), to… | 1. The upper stratum of the earth; the mold, or that compound substance which furnishes nutriment to plants, or which is particularly adapted to support and nourish them. 2. Land; country.
sowens: A nutritious article of food, much used in Scotland, made from the husk of the oat by a process not unlike that by which common starch is made; -- called flummery in England. [Written also sowans, and sowins.]
sourish: Somewhat sour; moderately acid; as, sourish fruit; a sourish taste.
soundingboard: 1. (Mus.) A thin board which propagates the sound in a piano, in a violin, and in some other musical instruments. 2. A board or structure placed behind or over a pulpit or rostrum to give distinctness to a speaker's voice. 3. pl. See Sound boarding, under Sound, a noise.
sociable: 1. Capable of being, or fit to be, united in one body or company; associable. They are sociable parts united into one body. Hooker. 2. Inclined to, or adapted for, society; | 1. A gathering of people for social purposes; an informal party or reception; as, a church sociable. [Colloq. U. S.] 2. A carriage having two double seats facing each other, and a box for the driver.
sowbane: The red goosefoot (Chenopodium rubrum), -- said to be fatal to swine.
sorry: 1. Grieved for the loss of some good; pained for some evil; feeling regret; -- now generally used to express light grief or affliction, but formerly often used to express deeper feeling. "I am sorry for my sins." Piers Plowman. Ye were made sorry after a godly manner. 2 Cor. vii. 9. I am sorry for thee, friend; 't is the duke's pleasure. Shak.
somniloquy: A talking in sleep; the talking of one in a state of somnipathy. Coleridge.
somal: A Hamitic people of East Central Africa.
socratism: The philosophy or the method of Socrates.
sostenuto: Sustained; -- applied to a movement or passage the sounds of which are to sustained to the utmost of the nominal value of the time; also, to a passage the tones of which are to be somewhat prolonged or protacted.
sodden: Boiled; seethed; also, soaked; heavy with moisture; saturated; as, sodden beef; sodden bread; sodden fields. | To be seethed; to become sodden.
sororize: To associate, or hold fellowship, as sisters; to have sisterly feelings; -- analogous to fraternize. [Recent & R.]
soporate: To lay or put to sleep; to stupefy. (old) Cudworth.
sodio: A combining form (also used adjectively) denoting the presence of sodium or one of its compounds.
socinianize: To cause to conform to Socinianism; to regulate by, or imbue with, the principles of Socinianism.
somnambulism: A condition of the nervous system in which an individual during sleep performs actions approppriate to the waking state; a state of sleep in which some of the senses and voluntary powers are partially awake; noctambulism.
soaking: Wetting thoroughly; drenching; as, a soaking rain. -- Soak"ing*ly, adv.
sowl: To pull by the ears; to drag about. (old) hak.
sororicide: The murder of one's sister; also, one who murders or kills one's own sister. Johnson.
soliped: A mammal having a single hoof on each foot, as the horses and asses; a solidungulate. [Written also solipede.] The solipeds, or firm-hoofed animals, as horses, asses, and mules, etc., -- they are, also, in mighty number. Sir T. Browne.
soothe: 1. To assent to as true. (old) Testament of Love. 2. To assent to; to comply with; to gratify; to humor by compliance; to please with blandishments or soft words; to flatter. sociological: Of or pertaining to sociology, or social science. -- So`ci*o*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
soapwort: A common plant (Saponaria officinalis) of the Pink family; -- so called because its bruised leaves, when agitated in water, produce a lather like that from soap. Called also Bouncing Bet.
souchong: A kind of black tea of a fine quality.
sorites: An abridged form of stating of syllogisms in a series of propositions so arranged that the predicate of each one that precedes forms the subject of each one that follows, and the conclusion unites the subject of the first proposition with the predicate of the last proposition, as in following example; -- The soul is a thinking agent;
sodalite: A mineral of a white to blue or gray color, occuring commonly in dodecahedrons, also massive. It is a silicate of alumina and soda with some chlorine.
soph: A contraction of Soph ister. [Colloq.] | A contraction of Sophomore. [Colloq.]
sociality: The quality of being social; socialness.
somnambulist: A person who is subject to somnambulism; one who walks in his sleep; a sleepwalker; a noctambulist.
solicitorgeneral: The second law officer in the government of Great Britain; also, a similar officer under the United States government, who is associated with the attorney-general; also, the chief law officer of some of the States.
soaproot: A perennial herb (Gypsophila Struthium) the root of which is used in Spain as a substitute for soap.
solenoglypha: A suborder of serpents including those which have tubular erectile fangs, as the viper and rattlesnake. See Fang.
sodomite: 1. An inhabitant of Sodom. 2. One guilty of sodomy.
southcottian: A follower of Joanna Southcott (1750-1814), an Englishwoman who, professing to have received a miraculous calling, preached and prophesied, and committed many impious absurdities.
soldering: from Solder, v. t. Soldering iron, Soldering tool, an instrument for soldering, consisting of a bit or bolt of copper having a pointed or wedge-shaped end, and furnished with a handle.
soliddrawn: Drawn out from a heated solid bar, as by a process of spiral rolling which first hollows the bar and then expands the cavity by forcing the bar over a pointed mandrel fixed in front of the rolls; - - said of a weldless tube.
soufflee: Filled with air by beating, and baked; as, an omelette soufflé.
sonification: The act of producing sound, as the stridulation of insects.
sovereignty: The quality or state of being sovereign, or of being a sovereign; the exercise of, or right to exercise, supreme power; dominion; sway; supremacy; independence; also, that which is sovereign; a sovereign state; as, Italy was formerly divided into many sovereignties. Woman desiren to have sovereignty As well over their husband as over their love. Chaucer.
softsteel: Steel low in carbon; mild steel; ingot iron.
somnambular: Of or pertaining to somnambulism; somnambulistic. Mrs. Browning.
sojourn: To dwell for a time; to dwell or live in a place as a temporary resident or as a stranger, not considering the place as a permanent habitation; to delay; to tarry. | A temporary residence, as that of a traveler in a foreign land. Though long detained In that obscure sojourn. Milton.
somewhere: In some place unknown or not specified; in one place or another. "Somewhere nigh at hand." Milton.
softening: from Soften, v. Softening of the brain, or Cerebral softening (Med.), a localized softening of the brain substance, due to hemorrhage or inflammation. Three varieties, distinguished by their color and representing different stages of the morbid process, are known respectively as red, yellow, and white, softening.
sory: Green vitriol, or some earth imregnated with it.
sonless: Being without a son. Marston. As no baron who was sonless could give a husband to his daughter, save with his lord's consent. J. R. Green.
socotrine: Of or pertaining to Socotra, an island in the Indian Ocean, on the east coast of Africa. -- n. A native or inhabitant of Socotra.
solidate: To make solid or firm. (old) Cowley.
sorner: One who obtrudes himself on another for bed and board. [Scot.] De Quncey.
souded: United; consolidated; made firm; strengthened. (old) O martyr souded for virginity! Chaucer.
soporiferous: Causing sleep; somniferous; soporific. "Soporiferous medicine." Swift. --- Sop`o*rif"er*ous*ly, adv. -- Sop`o*rif"er*ous*ness, n.
solenaceous: Of or pertaining to the solens or family Solenidæ.
somniloquence: The act of talking in one's sleep; somniloquism.
sorghum: (a) A genus of grasses, properly limited to two species, Sorghum Halepense, the Arabian millet, or Johnson grass (see Johnson grass), and S. vulgare, the Indian millet (see Indian millet, under Indian). (b) A variety of Sorghum vulgare, grown for its saccharine juice; the Chinese sugar cane.
soredium: A patch of granular bodies on the surface of the thallus of lichens.
somatotropism: A directive influence exercised by a mass of matter upon growing organs. Encyc. Brit.
solder: A metal or metallic alloy used when melted for uniting adjacent metallic edges or surfaces; a metallic coment. Hence, anything which unites or cements. Hard solder, a solder which fuses only at a red… | 1. To unite (metallic surfaces or edges) by the intervention of a more fusible metal or metallic alloy applied when melted; to join by means of metallic cement. 2. To mend; to patch up.
solemnity: 1. A rite or ceremony performed with religious reverence; religious or ritual ceremony; as, the solemnity of a funeral, a sacrament. Great was the cause; our old solemnities From no blind zeal or fond tradition rise, But saved from death, our Argives yearly pay These grateful honors to the god of day. Pope. 2. ceremony adapted to impress with awe.
sooty: 1. Of or pertaining to soot; producing soot; soiled by soot. "Fire of sooty coal." Milton. 2. Having a dark brown or black color like soot; fuliginous; dusky; dark. | To black or foul with soot. Sootied with noisome smoke. Chapman.
soliloquy: 1. The act of talking to one's self; a discourse made by one in solitude to one's self; monologue. Lovers are always allowed the comfort of soliloquy. Spectator. 2. A written composition, reciting what it is supposed a person says to himself. The whole poem is a soliloquy. Prior.
solomon: One of the kings of Israel, noted for his superior wisdom and magnificent reign; hence, a very wise man. -- Sol`o*mon"ic, a. Solomon's seal (Bot.), a perennial liliaceous plant of the genus Polygonatum, having simple erect or curving stems rising from thick and knotted rootstocks, and with white or greenish nodding flowers.
softener: One who, or that which, softens. [Written also, less properly, softner.]
soldierwood: A showy leguminous plant (Calliandra purpurea) of the West Indies. The flowers have long tassels of purple stamens.
soldanrie: The country ruled by a soldan, or sultan. [Poet.] Sir W. Scott.
sorema: A heap of carpels belonging to one flower.
sorcering: Act or practice of using sorcery.
solstice: 1. A stopping or standing still of the sun. (old) Sir T. Browne. 2. (Astron.) (a) The point in the ecliptic at which the sun is farthest from the equator, north or south, namely, the first point of the sign Cancer and the first point of the sign Capricorn, the former being the summer solstice, latter the winter solstice, in northern latitudes;
sociate: An associate. (old) As for you, Dr. Reynolds, and your sociates. Fuller.
soundingballoon: An unmanned balloon sent aloft for meteorological or aëronautic purposes.
sourde: To have origin or source; to rise; to spring. (old) Now might men ask whereof that pride sourdeth. Chaucer.
sonde: That which is sent; a message or messenger; hence, also, a visitation of providence; an affliction or trial. (old) Ye have enough, parde, of Goddes sond. Chaucer.
sociability: The quality of being sociable; sociableness.
soothsayer: 1. One who foretells events by the art of soothsaying; a prognosticator. 2. (Zoöl.) A mantis.
souterly: Of or pertaining to a cobbler or cobblers; like a cobbler; hence, vulgar; low. (old)
socialist: One who advocates or practices the doctrines of socialism. | Pertaining to, or of the nature of, socialism.
sopping: more recent version of soppy. Used esp. in phrase sopping wet.
sootiness: The quality or state of being sooty; fuliginousness. Johnson.
somnolism: The somnolent state induced by animal magnetism. Thomas (Med. Dict.).
sophomoric: Of or pertaining to a sophomore; resembling a sophomore; hence, pretentious; inflated in style or manner; as, sophomoric affectation. [U. S.]
sorosis: A woman's club; an association of women. [U. S.] | A fleshy fruit formed by the consolidation of many flowers with their receptacles, ovaries, etc., as the breadfruit, mulberry, and pineapple.
somniatory: Pertaining to sleep or dreams; somnial. [Obs. or R.] Urquhart.
solar: A loft or upper chamber; a garret room. (old) [Written also soler, solere, sollar.] Oxf. Gloss. | 1. solitarian: A hermit; a solitary. (old) Sir R. Twisden.
somaj: A society; a congregation; a worshiping assembly, or church, esp. of the Brahmo-somaj. [India]
somberly: In a somber manner; sombrously; gloomily; despondingly.
sonometer: 1. (Physiol.) An instrument for exhibiting the transverse vibrations of cords, and ascertaining the relations between musical notes. An instrument for testing the hearing capacity.
soubise: 1. [F.] A sauce made of white onions and melted butter mixed with velouté sauce. 2. A kind of cravat worn by men in the late 18th century.
solitaire: 1. A person who lives in solitude; a recluse; a hermit. Pope. 2. A single diamond in a setting; also, sometimes, a precious stone of any kind set alone. sob: To sigh with a sudden heaving of the breast, or with a kind of convulsive motion; to sigh with tears, and with a convulsive drawing in of the breath. Any sorrowful cry or sound.
solecize: To commit a solecism. Dr. H. More.
sodomy: Carnal copulation in a manner against nature; buggery. Gen. xix. 5.
sors: A lot; also, a kind of divination by means of lots. sorbition: The act of drinking or sipping. (old)
sophisticated: Adulterated; not pure; not genuine. So truth, while only one supplied the state, Grew scare and dear, and yet sophisticate. Dryden.
sophister: 1. A sophist. See Sophist. (old) Hooker. 2. (Eng. Univ.) A student who is advanced beyond the first year of his residence. Note: The entire course at the university consists of three years and one… | To maintain by sophistry, or by a fallacious argument. (old) obham.
soon: 1. In a short time; shortly after any time specified or supposed; as, soon after sunrise. "Sooner said than done." Old Proverb. "As soon as it might be." Chaucer. Promptly; quickly; easily.
soyle: To solve, to clear up; as, to soyl all other texts. (old) Tyndate.
soldiership: Military qualities or state; martial skill; behavior becoming a soldier. Shak.
sorb: (a) The wild service tree (Pyrus torminalis) of Europe; also, the rowan tree. (b) The fruit of these trees. Sorb apple, the fruit of the sorb, or wild service tree. -- Sorb tree, the wild service tree.
somersault: A leap in which a person turns his heels over his head and lights upon his feet; a turning end over end. [Written also summersault, sommerset, summerset, etc.] "The vaulter's sombersalts." Donne. Now I'll only Make him break his neck in doing a sommerset. Beau. & Fl.
sorter: One who, or that which, sorts.
sorrel: Of a yellowish or redish brown color; as, a sorrel horse. | A yellowish or redish brown color.
sorus: One of the fruit dots, or small clusters of sporangia, on the back of the fronds of ferns.
songster: 1. One who sings; one skilled in singing; -- not often applied to human beings. 2. (Zoöl.) A singing bird.
sound: The air bladder of a fish; as, cod sounds are an esteemed article of food. | A cuttlefish. (old) Ainsworth.
sober: 1. Temperate in the use of spirituous liquors; habitually temperate; as, a sober man. That we may hereafter live a godly, righteous, and sober life, to the glory of Thy holy name. Bk. of Com. Prayer. | To make sober. There shallow draughts intoxicate the brain, And drinking largely sobers us again. Pope.
sou: An old French copper coin, equivalent in value to, and now displaced by, the five-centime piece (sou.
sop: 1. Anything steeped, or dipped and softened, in any liquid; especially, something dipped in broth or liquid food, and intended to be eaten. He it is to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it. | To steep or dip in any liquid.
soulili: A long-tailed, crested Javan monkey (Semnopithecus mitratus). The head, the crest, and the upper surface of the tail, are black.
souled: Furnished with a soul; possessing soul and feeling; -- used chiefly in composition; as, great-souled Hector. "Grecian chiefs . . . largely souled." Dryden.
solmization: The act of sol-faing. soundboard: A sounding-board. To many a row of pipes the sound-board breathes. Milton.
solicitation: 1. The act of soliciting; earnest request; persistent asking; importunity. 2. Excitement; invitation; as, the solicitation of the senses. Locke.
soapiness: Quality or state of being soapy.
solenodon: Either one of two species of singular West Indian insectivores, allied to the tenrec. One species (Solendon paradoxus), native of St. Domingo, is called also agouta; the other (S. Cubanus), found in Cuba, is called almique.
solere: A loft or garret. See Solar, n. Sir W. Scott.
soboles: (a) A shoot running along under ground, forming new plants at short distances. (b) A sucker, as of tree or shrub.
song: 1. That which is sung or uttered with musical modulations of the voice, whether of a human being or of a bird, insect, etc. "That most ethereal of all sounds, the song of crickets." Hawthorne. 2. A lyrical poem adapted to vocal music; a ballad. 3. More generally, any poetical strain; a poem.
solidary: Having community of interests and responsibilities. Men are solidary, or copartners; and not isolated. M. Arnold.
solifidian: One who maintains that faith alone, without works, is sufficient for justification; -- opposed to nullifidian. Hammond. | Holding the tenets of Solifidians; of or pertaining to the solifidians.
sond: That which is sent; a message or messenger; hence, also, a visitation of providence; an affliction or trial. (old) Ye have enough, parde, of Goddes sond. Chaucer.
sol: 1. The sun. 2. (Alchem.) Gold; -- so called from its brilliancy, color, and value. Chaucer. | (a) A syllable applied in solmization to the note G, or to the fifth tone of any diatonic scale. (b) The tone itself.
